analysis.title: Pitney Bowes (PBI): 3Q First Take: Modest revenue shortfall mitigated by margin upside and an increase to the full-year revenue guide
key_insights: PBI 3Q26 revenue of $456.2mn fell 0.8% y/y, worse than GS estimate of -0.4% and FactSet consensus of -0.3%. The decline improved from -2% in 2Q.

Adjusted EBIT margin expanded 160 bps y/y to 25.0%, above GS forecast of 22.4% and consensus of 22.3%, driven by SendTech cost reduction initiatives and efficiencies, partly offset by lower revenue per piece in Presort and higher fuel and transportation costs.
3Q EPS of $0.42 beat GS estimate of $0.34 and FactSet consensus of $0.35.
SendTech revenue fell 2% y/y on continued mailing install base erosion, partly offset by higher equipment sales. Presort revenue rose 1% y/y on 4% higher volumes from new client wins.
FY26 revenue guide raised to $1,830-1,860mn from $1,800-1,860mn, a y/y decline of 1.7-3.3% (1.7-4.9% prior), with the midpoint decline at 2.5% vs 3.3% previously.
FY26 operating income guide narrowed to $450-470mn from $445-475mn. Midpoint operating margin is 24.9% vs 25.1% prior. FY26 EPS guide narrowed to $1.58-1.67 from $1.55-1.70.

GS says the guidance points to stable consensus revisions for revenue and operating margins and negative revisions for EPS. Pre-print, GS forecast FY26 EPS of $1.68, equal to FactSet consensus of $1.68, both above the top of the new guide range.
PBI cut debt by $148mn and repurchased $17mn of shares in the quarter.

GS expects the 29 October earnings call to focus on mailing volume declines and install-base erosion, Presort volume recovery and revenue per piece, sustainability of SendTech margin expansion, and updates on the strategic review.

GS rates PBI Neutral with a 12-month price target of $17.30 (6.75x NTM+1YR EBITDA of $581mn, NTM net debt $1,536mn, 138mn NTM shares). The stock closed at $17.44, implying 0.8% downside. The multiple is below the Business Services peer median of 9.0x due to mail secular headwinds, near-term revenue declines and leverage.

market_movers.rationale: Price target is unchanged from the 30 July 2026 level of $17.30. The stock trades at $17.44, 0.8% above target. The 6.75x EBITDA multiple reflects mail secular decline and leverage.

earnings_insights: PBI 3Q26 reported revenue $456.2mn (-0.8% y/y) vs GS est $457.9mn (-0.4%) and FactSet consensus $458.2mn (-0.3%).
PBI 3Q26 adjusted EBIT $113.9mn, margin 25.0%, vs GS est $102.3mn (22.4%) and FactSet consensus $102.0mn (22.3%).
PBI 3Q26 reported EPS $0.42 vs GS est $0.34 and FactSet consensus $0.35.
FY26 guidance after the 3Q print: revenue $1,830-1,860mn (prior $1,800-1,860mn), operating income $450-470mn (prior $445-475mn), EPS $1.58-1.67 (prior $1.55-1.70).
Pre-print FY26 estimates: GS revenue $1,863mn, operating income $467mn, margin 25.1%, EPS $1.68. FactSet consensus revenue $1,848mn, operating income $458mn, margin 24.8%, EPS $1.68.
GS forward estimates: 4Q26E EPS $0.43, 1Q27E EPS $0.53, FY27E EPS $1.89, FY28E EPS $2.24. GS 3Q26 EPS estimate is shown as $0.34 in the quarterly table.
risk_factors: Structural declines in the US mail market.
Execution risk surrounding the ongoing strategic review.
Credit and interest rate risk from the leasing portfolio.
Upside risks: value creation from the strategic review, SendTech product innovation, organic and inorganic Presort share gains, and margin expansion from cost efficiency.
